5669.title: [M158] Adopt upstream GPU correctness fixes
5669.body:
[M158] Adopt upstream GPU correctness fixes (#5669)

Context: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/439
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5675
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1671411
Changes: https://github.com/google/skia/compare/75584a96108b2bf0b1c74b0536126fa4917b64a8...361c8326695a06b7492fb6eeeff803c0c92a2447

Adopt the merged m158 GPU bug fixes without a milestone or package-version
transition. Update the native gitlink and Component Governance identities;
the companion native PR carries the implementation changes.

~~ Respect affected ARM Vulkan device-loss teardown timing ~~

Some Mali drivers report idle completion before device teardown is safe.
Adopt the Ganesh and Graphite workaround that adds a 1 ms delay on the
relevant loss paths for ARM proprietary drivers from 42.0 through versions
below 56.0, rather than delaying ordinary successful submissions.

~~ Preserve hairline cap scale under reflected transforms ~~

A negative determinant previously selected a local-space unit outset for
zero-length square-capped hairlines, allowing reflected scales to enlarge
the cap. Adopt the signed inverse-determinant calculation and finite-result
guard for singular matrices and overflow.

~~ Select text-atlas samplers despite interpolation imprecision ~~

Ganesh's flat-varying hint is not a guarantee. Adopt rounding before the
integer sampler-index comparison in ordinary and LCD atlas lookups so
interpolation error does not select the wrong atlas.

~~ Bound Graphite clip recording within a render pass ~~

Account for effective undrawn clip elements when deciding to flush.
Because flushing resets clip recording, reject and log a draw whose clips
cannot fit a fresh pass instead of overflowing the pass structures.
The native update includes DeviceTestClipRenderStepLimits.

~~ Pin the actual native merge without changing the reviewed tree ~~

Pin mono/skia merge 7329f82be5f66b326acdfadbc87a62793e6d6dba rather
than leaving the parent on the temporary reviewed branch head. Its two
parents include reviewed head 365bf08330f18bbe64c5e9f84f251262afe7f371,
and both commits have tree 3bf18d50473a78bcfe982206ef0810e825aad412.

Keep the gitlink and mono/skia commitHash aligned while recording exact
upstream commit 361c8326695a06b7492fb6eeeff803c0c92a2447 separately.
Retain chrome/m158 and milestone 158; no managed declarations or version
inputs change in this parent PR.

Build 1671411 succeeded for the pre-repin parent source, including the
single Mac Catalyst retry after an agent-side .NET setup permission error.
Independent regeneration matched the generated bindings. The repin changes
native commit identity, not its tree; affected-device Vulkan loss behavior
was not specifically established by the integration review.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

5554.title: Update HarfBuzz to 15.0.0 and complete script constants
5554.body:
Update HarfBuzz to 15.0.0 and complete script constants (#5554)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/419
Changes: https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/compare/36cb489cb02ce4b92099669ba9f9bea348eff93f...35f656a1a2bab548ea7f54a6dd3fba2b09680d14

Keep the native HarfBuzz revision, packaged library identity and managed
bindings aligned while adopting 15.0.0. Complete the manually maintained
Script constants without replacing their existing struct-based API.

~~ Align the native upgrade with its package identity ~~

Adopt HarfBuzz revision 35f656a1a2bab548ea7f54a6dd3fba2b09680d14
through mono/skia#419. The native companion updates DEPS and the GN source
inventory for the added headers and test sources, including the change
from OT/Layout/types.hh to hb-ot-dual.hh.

Pin externals/skia and its matching governance registration to native
commit fb69790c17977edad0142d277435ec5514dd0f2d. Record HarfBuzz
15.0.0 and its exact revision and version-header evidence in cgmanifest.

Advance the native SONAME from 0.61440.0 to 0.61500.0. Reset the
HarfBuzzSharp file and NativeAssets package versions from 14.4.0.300 to
15.0.0: a native version upgrade establishes a new revision-zero bucket,
rather than continuing the previous version's milestone servicing range.
Keep the HarfBuzzSharp assembly version at 1.0.0.0 and retain the m158
SkiaSharp product versions.

The rebased source passed the macOS ARM64 native build and unfiltered
net10.0 console solution, including existing shaping and subsetting tests.

~~ Regenerate the deprecated font-face setter import ~~

HarfBuzz moves hb_font_set_face from hb-font.h to hb-deprecated.h and marks
it deprecated in favor of hb_font_create. The binding configuration
already excludes hb-deprecated.h, so regeneration removes the unused
internal hb_font_set_face declarations and delegate path.

Do not restore the import by hand or widen deprecated-header generation:
Font(Face) already constructs fonts through hb_font_create, and this
removal does not remove a public managed member. The current-head
binding-generation determinism check passes after regeneration.

~~ Complete named scripts without changing the Script programming model ~~

The native script list advanced while Script.fields.cs remained manually
maintained. Regenerating interop alone cannot repair that gap:
hb_script_t deliberately maps to UInt32 with generation disabled because
HarfBuzzSharp exposes a custom Script struct, not a generated enum.

Add 30 documented static readonly fields: Jurchen, ProtoCuneiform and Seal
from the updated native list, plus 27 previously omitted constants.
Preserve the 149 existing field declarations and values. The resulting
179 named tag values match the HB_TAG entries in the selected native
hb-script-list.h.

Keep the struct's parsing, numeric conversions and horizontal-direction
lookup intact. Document the manual synchronization requirement beside the
generator mapping so future native updates do not mistake disabled enum
generation for complete script coverage.

Add a theory case for each new field, asserting its numeric tag,
ToString output, Parse result and successful TryParse round-trip against
the native-backed parser.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

5634.title: [M158] Update SkiaSharp to Skia milestone 158
5634.body:
[M158] Update SkiaSharp to Skia milestone 158 (#5634)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/438
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5637
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/ce0fc683a40c6ba84d55072f31aa48d55c8f2131...f93fd1e432b85086477a6a1c21c1e560673d4a14

Adopt the m158 native engine as the 4.158 product line, keeping package,
assembly, native-library and governance identities consistent with the
selected Skia revision. Preserve the existing managed binding surface
while consuming the upstream engine update through the fork's C bridge.

~~ Pin the landed native merge without changing the reviewed tree ~~

Advance externals/skia from ce0fc683a40c6ba84d55072f31aa48d55c8f2131
to the actual mono/skia merge f93fd1e432b85086477a6a1c21c1e560673d4a14.
The native companion integrates chrome/m158 through
75584a96108b2bf0b1c74b0536126fa4917b64a8 while retaining the fork's
dependency policy, C bridge and platform compatibility adaptations.

The dependent repin in #5637 changes only the gitlink and matching
cgmanifest commitHash. The landed native commit has two parents and
directly includes reviewed b8af0ba51c9409bb2087e86a7461349c803b7170.
Both native commits have tree 435f794aa44e8ff7902239fdf24913783eda4837,
so recording the landed SHA does not substitute different native source
for the reviewed and built source.

The producing sync reports a passing Linux x64 native source build,
managed binding build and unfiltered console solution. Binding
regeneration reported no generated changes; this parent diff changes no
managed wrappers, generated bindings or C API declarations.

~~ Keep the 4.158 package line and native identity synchronized ~~

Change the Skia release and libSkiaSharp milestone from 157 to 158.
Keep the C API increment at zero and set the native SONAME to 158.0.0:
the milestone changes even though this update adds no C bridge exports.

Advance the SkiaSharp assembly/file version to 4.158.0.0 and the
SkiaSharp-family NuGet rows in VERSIONS.txt to 4.158.0. Set the Azure
SKIASHARP_VERSION variable to the same numeric package version so CI
does not identify the new milestone's packages as the previous line.
These are source version inputs, not a declaration that packages have
been published.

~~ Reserve the next HarfBuzzSharp milestone revision bucket ~~

Keep native HarfBuzz at 14.4.0, its SONAME at 0.61440.0 and the
HarfBuzzSharp assembly version at 1.0.0.0. Advance its file and NuGet
versions from 14.4.0.200 to 14.4.0.300.

The version policy reserves 100 revision values per Skia milestone
while the native HarfBuzz version stays unchanged. Moving to the next
bucket distinguishes the m158 package set without implying a native
HarfBuzz upgrade or consuming the previous milestone's servicing range.

~~ Record the exact upstream and Vulkan-Headers governance identities ~~

Update the Skia governance entry from chrome/m157 to chrome/m158 and
record upstream revision 75584a96108b2bf0b1c74b0536126fa4917b64a8.
Keep that upstream identity distinct from the mono/skia fork merge:
the git registration and submodule both use the actual landed fork SHA.

The native update advances Vulkan-Headers from 1.4.365 to 1.4.366.
Record revision 73814d006638aa00bd553215b054f0f02e457e22 in the
dependency registration, reviewed-identity URL and header-version source.
This keeps the manifest's version and revision evidence aligned with the
selected native DEPS pin rather than retaining the previous header
identity after the engine update.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

5620.title: Detect incomplete NuGet shipments in release audits
5620.body:
* Detect incomplete NuGet shipments in release audits

Check each shipment's source-controlled shipping package IDs and exact family versions, discover publication without the SkiaSharp anchor, and block Finish and replacement cuts until publication is complete. Reuse the completeness guard in Finish and expose missing versus unavailable evidence.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Keep publication documentation focused on operator guidance

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Use exact shipping inputs for historical package inventories

Exclude version rows whose projects were not yet included in the shipment's pack filter. Cover project inclusion changes with a committed-source fixture, so a newer VERSIONS entry does not falsely mark an older shipment partial.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Use tracked solution-filter casing in publishing tests

Match SkiaSharpSource.Windows.slnf so the inventory assertion also runs on case-sensitive Linux filesystems.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Keep intermediate unpublished stable cuts visible in release reports

Show the latest complete shipment alongside partial publication and retain older missing stable cuts for review without changing release action gates.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Add task-focused release audit checks and milestone ranges

Select Upstream, Prepare, Finish, or NuGet without fetching unrelated checks. Keep the full audit as the default and retain all prerequisite gates for Prepare. Expand inclusive same-major ranges, preserve per-line failures, and distinguish unchecked facts from healthy results.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Assert Finish reporting independently of console table wrapping

Use the explicit release-action field instead of relying on a host-specific table row layout.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Trim release audit documentation to usage and safety requirements

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
